principle: Memory is actor-specific recollection derived from events/knowledge; it is not World Truth and is not guaranteed perfect.

states.recent_detailed: fresh memory with relatively rich retrievable detail
states.consolidated_relevant: stable memory with important detail retained
states.gist_retained: core meaning remains while detail is lost
states.reinterpreted: meaning/emotional interpretation changed without changing the past event
states.inactive_or_forgotten: not normally retrievable without valid reconstruction cues

rules: Not every experienced event requires a persistent detailed memory.
Routine episodes may be summarized or aggregated.
Loss of detail does not authorize fabrication.
Gist may persist after details fade.
Shared events do not create identical memories in different characters.
A memory may be inaccurate, incomplete, emotionally colored or sincerely misinterpreted.
Reinterpretation changes the actor's understanding, not the authoritative past event.
Forgetting does not erase external commitments, records, injuries, relationships or world consequences.
Evidence or another person's reminder may support reconstruction but does not force perfect recall.
LOD and save/load do not reroll memory.
AI may use only available relevant memories and may express uncertainty or lack of recall.
AI cannot invent missing shared history or missing details to improve dialogue.
